19	import java.util.Collection;
20	
21	import org.springframework.orm.ObjectRetrievalFailureException;
22	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Utility methods for handling entities. Separate from the BaseEntity class mainly because of dependency on the
26	 * ORM-associated ObjectRetrievalFailureException.
27	 *
28	 * @author Juergen Hoeller
29	 * @author Sam Brannen
30	 * @see org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity
31	 * @since 29.10.2003
32	 */
33	public abstract class EntityUtils {
34	
35	    /**
36	     * Look up the entity of the given class with the given id in the given collection.
37	     *
38	     * @param entities    the collection to search
39	     * @param entityClass the entity class to look up
40	     * @param entityId    the entity id to look up
41	     * @return the found entity
42	     * @throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException if the entity was not found
43	     */
44	    public static <T extends BaseEntity> T getById(Collection<T> entities, Class<T> entityClass, int entityId)
45	        throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException {
46	        for (T entity : entities) {
47	            if (entity.getId() == entityId && entityClass.isInstance(entity)) {
48	                return entity;
49	            }
50	        }
51	        throw new ObjectRetrievalFailureException(entityClass, entityId);
52	    }
53	
54	}

content.text:
No leftover references. The restructuring is complete.

## What I did

I prepared the code so the upcoming E.164 change has a natural home, without implementing the change or altering any current behavior.

**The problem:** Telephone handling lived as a one-line private helper (`normalizeTelephone`) inside `OwnerRestControllerV1`. Implementing E.164 directly there would have piled substantial parsing/validation logic (`toE164`, `toE164Quietly`) into the controller and bloated `addOwner`/`updateOwner`/`isTelephoneInUse` — the exact classes flagged as over-full.

**The restructuring:**
- Extracted telephone canonicalization into a dedicated Spring `@Component`, `util/TelephoneNormalizer`, with a single `normalize(String)` method carrying the current behavior exactly (strip non-digits, null-safe). This is the `util` package that already hosts reusable helpers, and component scanning from the root `@SpringBootApplication` wires it automatically.
- Injected it into `OwnerRestControllerV1` via the constructor (matching the existing mapper/service injection style) and had `addOwner` and `isTelephoneInUse` delegate to it.
- Removed the now-redundant private `normalizeTelephone`.

Now the E.164 work lands by evolving one focused component (swapping its algorithm, adding a quiet variant) plus the exception/handler pair in `rest.advice` — the controller stays thin. I deliberately left `normalizeEmail`, `updateOwner`'s current non-normalizing behavior, the `Owner`/OpenAPI validation, and the exception layer untouched, since those belong to the change itself.

**Verification:** Full suite before and after is byte-identical — the one genuine current test (`errorRejectsUnformattable`) still passes, and the two `AcceptanceTest` cases that assert `+61…`/`+64…` still fail exactly as before because they are the acceptance spec for the *not-yet-implemented* E.164 change. The refactored code compiles and boots the full Spring context (the MockMvc test ran), confirming the new bean wires correctly.
